days.title: Arrival in Tokyo
days.tagline: Touch down at Narita. Neon lights and konbini runs await.
highlights: 18:30 — Land at Narita Airport
Narita Express to Shibuya — 75 min, ¥3,250
Buy Suica IC cards at the airport kiosk
Check into hotel. Light konbini dinner — onigiri is your new best friend
days.food: Konbini onigiri — umeboshi, kombu fillings are naturally GF + vegan. Available 24/7.
days.tip: Withdraw yen at 7-Eleven ATMs — best rates, English menus. Japan runs on cash.

days.title: TeamLab & Harajuku
days.tagline: Immersive digital art, then the sensory overload of Shibuya at night.
highlights: TeamLab Borderless at Azabudai Hills — ¥3,800, book 2 months ahead
Meiji Shrine — ancient forest in the heart of the city
Harajuku & Takeshita Street — pop culture, fashion, chaos
Shibuya Crossing at dusk — you live here. Golden Gai after dark.

activities.name: Dinner — Ain Soph Journey (vegan, GF options)

transport.note: All within central Tokyo, use Suica

days.food: Ain Soph Journey (Shinjuku) — fully vegan, GF options. Afuri ramen in Harajuku — ask for tamari.
days.tip: Wear dark clothing at TeamLab — projections look best on black. Book tickets the moment they open (2 months ahead).

days.title: Kamakura
days.tagline: 13th-century capital. Giant Buddha, ocean temples, island at sunset.
highlights: JR Yokosuka Line from Shibuya — 60 min, ¥940
Tsurugaoka Hachimangū shrine → Komachi-dōri street
Kōtoku-in — the Great Buddha, 13m tall, cast in 1252
Hase-dera Temple — ocean views, hydrangeas in May
Enoden train to Enoshima Island — caves, shrine, panoramic views
days.food: Bowls Kamakura (plant-based café near Hase). Look for vegetable tempura sets (note: batter has gluten).
days.tip: Time your visit to catch golden hour at Enoshima observation tower.

days.title: Mt Fuji
days.tagline: The iconic pagoda-and-peak view. Fuji is famously shy — go early.
highlights: Highway bus from Shibuya → Kawaguchiko — 2 hrs, ¥2,200
Chureito Pagoda — 398 steps to THE photo. Best light before noon.
Kawaguchiko Ropeway to Mt Tenjō — panoramic Fuji + lake view
Walk the north shore of Lake Kawaguchi — Fuji reflected in water
days.food: Limited veg/GF options around Kawaguchiko. Bring snacks from Tokyo. Rice dishes at lakeside restaurants.
days.tip: Clouds roll in by midday almost daily. The early bus is non-negotiable.

days.title: Tokyo → Kumamoto
days.tagline: A quick flight south. By lunch, you're in Kyushu.
highlights: Flight: Haneda → Kumamoto — 1h50, arrive by lunch
Limousine bus from Shibuya to Haneda (30 min, ¥1,300)
Kumamoto Castle — rebuilt after 2016 earthquake, stunning stone walls
Shimotori covered arcade — Kumamoto's beating heart
Whole afternoon free to explore — way more time than the 6hr shinkansen
days.food: Kumamoto is famous for horse meat (basashi) — not for you, but the veggie izakayas near Shimotori are excellent. Try tofu steak sets.
days.tip: Book HND→KMJ flight early — ANA Super Value or JAL Special Saver can drop to ¥8,000–12,000 if booked 75+ days ahead.

days.title: Mt Aso & Bike Ride
days.tagline: Active volcano, vast caldera, then e-bikes through landscapes most tourists never see.
highlights: JR Hōhi Line → Aso Station — 75 min through mountains
Morning: Bokuya Rides guided e-bike through protected grasslands
Rolling hills, volcanic panoramas, thrilling downhill return
Afternoon: Nakadake Crater — steaming vents, turquoise lake (if accessible)
Kusasenri — vast green meadows inside the caldera
days.food: Limited veggie options in Aso area. Bring snacks from Kumamoto konbini. Rice-bowl restaurants for GF.
days.tip: Book Bokuya Rides at asocalderatourism.com. Start with the ride while legs are fresh. Helmets provided.

days.title: Amakusa Beach Day
days.tagline: Crystal-clear waters and island bridges. Leave the volcano behind — today is sea and sand.
highlights: Rent a car or join a tour — Amakusa is 2 hours south across five bridges
Amakusa Gokyo (Five Bridges) — iconic chain linking mainland to the islands
Shirahama Beach — white sand, turquoise water, almost no tourists
Fresh seafood lunch at the port — Amakusa is famous for kuruma-ebi (tiger prawns)
Dolphin watching cruise — pods of wild Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphins year-round
Golden hour drive back across the bridges

activities.name: Explore Sakitsu village & church
activities.note: UNESCO World Heritage — hidden Christian site

days.food: Amakusa sea urchin and kuruma-ebi are legendary. Port restaurants serve the freshest seafood in Kyushu. For veggie options, bring snacks — choices are limited in rural Amakusa.
days.tip: Dolphin watching has 98% sighting rate year-round. Book at Amakusa Dolphin Center. Best light for the Five Bridges is golden hour on the return drive.

days.title: Kurokawa Onsen
days.tagline: Mountain onsen village. Soak in open-air baths hidden among cedar forests.
highlights: Bus from Kumamoto Sakuramachi → Kurokawa Onsen — 2.5 hrs through mountains
Rotenburo meguri — wooden pass (¥1,500) for 3 outdoor baths of your choice
Wander the village: cedar-lined paths, stone bridges, steam rising everywhere
Each ryokan has a unique bath — forest views, river-side, cave, rock formations
Evening return to Kumamoto — or linger for golden hour at the village

activities.name: Arrive Kurokawa, buy Nyuto Tegata pass
Village walk — bridges, steam, cedar paths

days.food: Limited options in Kurokawa. Tofu Kissho for handmade tofu dishes (vegan-friendly, soy sauce contains wheat — bring tamari). Pack snacks from Kumamoto konbini.
days.tip: Rotenburo meguri pass works at 28 participating ryokan baths. Bring a small towel (or buy one). Onsen etiquette: wash before entering, no swimwear, tattoos usually OK in Kurokawa.

days.title: Kumamoto → Onomichi
days.tagline: Shinkansen north. A hillside port town of cats, temples, and sea views.
highlights: Kumamoto → Hakata → Fukuyama → Onomichi — 3.5 hrs total
Optional: 2-hr Hiroshima Peace Memorial detour en route
Senkoji Ropeway — hilltop park overlooking the Seto Inland Sea
Cat Alley (Neko no Hosomichi) — narrow paths with feline street art
Reserve bikes at Onomichi terminal for tomorrow's Shimanami Kaido
days.food: Onomichi ramen is the local specialty (not veggie-friendly). Try Komichi Café near Cat Alley for lighter fare.
days.tip: If you can spare 2 hrs, detour to Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park en route. It's one of the most powerful experiences in Japan.

days.title: Shimanami Kaido → Osaka
days.tagline: 70 km across 6 islands. Then straight to Japan's kitchen.
highlights: 06:30 — Send bags via takkyubin to Osaka hotel (~¥2,500/bag)
07:00 — Pick up e-bikes, ferry to Mukaishima
Ride across 6 islands — soaring bridges, Seto Inland Sea blue
Stop at Setoda, Omishima shrines, beaches along the way
~15:00 — Drop bikes at Imabari terminal
Imabari → Okayama → Shin-Osaka — train ~3.5 hrs. Arrive ~19:00.

activities.name: Send bags via takkyubin
activities.note: per bag, arrives next day at Osaka hotel

activities.name: Pick up e-bikes at Onomichi terminal
Arrive Osaka, check into Namba hotel

transport.note: Ride Onomichi → Imabari (70km), then train to Osaka

days.food: Pack snacks before starting. Setoda has Dolce gelato shop. Omishima has mikan everything. Konbini stops on islands.
days.tip: Takkyubin: drop bags at any konbini or Yamato office by morning. Follow the blue line on the road. E-bikes worth every yen.

days.title: Osaka — Dōtonbori & Shinsekai
days.tagline: Neon canals, retro towers, and the art of eating till you drop.
highlights: Sleep in — your legs deserve it after yesterday
Dōtonbori — the neon-lit canal, Glico Running Man sign
Shinsekai — retro district under Tsutenkaku Tower
Street food crawl — takoyaki, okonomiyaki, yakiimo
Hozenji Yokocho at dusk — stone-paved alley, tiny restaurants

activities.name: Late start — rest day for legs

days.food: Paprika Shokudo Vegan (Namba). Green Earth (Shinsaibashi). For GF okonomiyaki, ask 'kome-ko de dekimasu ka?' (rice flour?).
days.tip: Osaka's motto is kuidaore — eat till you drop. Dōtonbori at night is pure electricity.

days.title: Osaka — Castle & Markets
days.tagline: Castle parks, market stalls, and the city that never stops eating.
highlights: Osaka Castle — 8-story keep, panoramic city views, ¥600
Walk through Castle Park — beautiful in mid-May greenery
Kuromon Market — 'Osaka's Kitchen', browse 170+ stalls
Shinsaibashi arcade — covered shopping stretching for blocks
days.food: Kuromon Market — look for fresh fruit, pickles, rice dishes. Mochi (glutinous rice ≠ gluten!) is naturally GF.
days.tip: Kuromon Market before 2pm — stalls close early. Supermarket bento after 7pm is 30-50% off.

days.title: Kyoto
days.tagline: Thousands of torii gates. Gold temples. Bamboo forests. Geisha at dusk.
highlights: JR Special Rapid to Kyoto — 30 min, ¥580
Fushimi Inari — go before 9am. Thousands of vermillion gates.
Kinkaku-ji — gold-leaf temple reflected in mirror pond
Arashiyama Bamboo Grove → Tenryū-ji → Togetsukyo Bridge
Gion at dusk — traditional machiya, geiko quarter
days.food: Kyoto has the best vegan scene in Japan. Shigetsu at Tenryū-ji (shōjin ryōri, ¥3,300–5,500). Mumokuteki Café. Falafel Garden (Gion).
days.tip: Fushimi Inari at dawn is life-changing. The first tunnel of gates, almost empty, almost holy.

days.title: Osaka → Tokyo
days.tagline: Final bullet train. Choose your Tokyo finale.
highlights: Morning: last Osaka stroll — pick up any remaining omiyage
Shinkansen Shin-Osaka → Tokyo — 2h45, ¥13,870
Option A: Asakusa — Sensō-ji, Tokyo's oldest temple
Option B: Akihabara — electronics, anime, retro gaming
Farewell dinner — Golden Gai or Michelin-star shōjin ryōri
days.food: Daigo near Shiba Park — 2-Michelin-star Buddhist vegan. Book ahead. Or casual Golden Gai.
days.tip: For a special last meal: Daigo is extraordinary. Otherwise, kaiten-zushi (conveyor belt sushi) — kappa, avocado, inari are veggie.

days.title: Departure
days.tagline: One last Tokyo morning. Then Narita. Then memories.
highlights: Tsukiji Outer Market — breakfast stalls, tamagoyaki, fresh fruit
Last shopping — Tokyo Station omiyage shops are incredible
Japanese Kit-Kats, matcha sweets, furoshiki wrapping cloths
19:00 — Narita Express to airport
22:50 — ✈️ Fly home to Warsaw. Sayonara, Japan.
days.food: Stock up on snacks at Narita — excellent selection. Senbei (rice crackers, GF!), mochi, regional KitKats.
days.tip: Tax-free shopping: ¥5,000+ at participating stores = ~10% savings. Don't open sealed items before leaving Japan.

jrPassAnalysis.recommendation: Definitely buy individual tickets. With Tokyo→Kumamoto now a flight, your shinkansen legs are only Kumamoto→Onomichi (¥13,000) and Osaka→Tokyo (¥13,870) plus local trains. The 7-day pass (¥50,000) costs more than your actual train spend. Individual tickets + Nozomi access is the clear winner.
jrPassAnalysis.note: No JR Pass needed. Individual shinkansen tickets can be booked at JR ticket counters (midori no madoguchi) or via SmartEX app.

restaurants.note: Curated for vegetarian/vegan travelers with celiac-level gluten allergy. GF = gluten-free. Always carry a Japanese allergy card and tamari packets.
restaurants.allergyCardJp: 私はセリアック病です。小麦・大麦・ライ麦を食べられません。醤油の代わりにたまりを使ってください。
restaurants.allergyCardEn: I have celiac disease. I cannot eat wheat, barley, or rye. Please use tamari instead of soy sauce.
safeFoods: Onigiri — umeboshi, kombu, nattō fillings (check labels for wheat)
Yakiimo — roasted sweet potato from street vendors
Fresh fruit — Japan's fruit is extraordinary
Tofu (hiyayakko/yudofu) — ask for tamari instead of soy sauce
dangerFoods: Soy sauce (shōyu) — contains wheat. Request tamari.
Ramen/udon/soba noodles — wheat (soba is buckwheat + wheat mix)
Dashi broth — usually bonito (fish), ask for kombu dashi
Okonomiyaki — wheat batter unless rice flour specified

kumamoto.survivalTips: Kumamoto is rural — GF options are genuinely limited. Stock up at konbini: plain onigiri (ume/kombu), edamame, fresh fruit, yakiimo. For Kurokawa day trip, pack snacks from Kumamoto.

spots.name: Komedoko Shokudo
spots.mustTry: Vegan GF ramen with rice flour noodles — your best bet in Onomichi
spots.note: Owner actively develops GF dishes. Waterfront views. Request advance notice for GF prep. This is the one reliable option.

spots.name: Kameyama Goya (Innoshima Island)
spots.mustTry: Green curry (verify no fish sauce) or pho with vegetable broth
spots.note: Only real island restaurant option. Confirm GF and ask about fish sauce in curries. Scenic cycling café stop.

whatToPack: Onigiri from Onomichi konbini (grab 4-5 before starting)
Individual tamari packets (for any rice dishes you find)
cyclingFuelGuide.konbiniStops: Lawson/FamilyMart/7-Eleven every 15-20km along route. Safe bets: rice balls (check for wheat - 小麦), edamame, bananas, Pocari Sweat.
cyclingFuelGuide.tip: Use Google Translate camera mode to scan konbini labels for 小麦 (wheat). Kanji is your friend.

days.title: Nara Day Trip
days.tagline: Ancient capital, giant Buddha, sacred deer. The day trip that got its own day.
days.splitNote: Jacek + Ola take the Shinkansen to Tokyo this morning. You stay in Osaka and head to Nara.
highlights: JR Namba → Nara — 45 min, ¥580
Tōdai-ji — the world's largest wooden building, housing a 15m bronze Buddha
Nara Park — over 1,200 free-roaming deer, sacred messengers of the gods
Kōfuku-ji — five-story pagoda, one of Japan's oldest temple complexes
Kasuga-taisha shrine — 3,000 stone lanterns lining the approach
Return to Osaka for evening

activities.name: Say goodbye to Jacek + Ola at Osaka station

days.food: Nara has more GF options than you'd expect. Look for mochi (rice-based, GF), kaki no ha sushi (persimmon leaf sushi — skip the soy sauce or use your tamari). Avoid anything with dashi broth unless you confirm it's kombu-only.
days.tip: Deer biscuits (shika senbei, ¥200) are sold at stalls everywhere. The deer know how to bow — if you bow first, they bow back. Don't tease them though, they WILL headbutt you.

days.title: Osaka → Kyoto — Higashiyama
days.tagline: Trading neon for tradition. Three days in Japan's cultural heart.
highlights: JR Special Rapid to Kyoto — 30 min, ¥580
Kiyomizu-dera — iconic wooden terrace with panoramic views
Ninenzaka → Sannenzaka — traditional streets with pagoda views
Hōkan-ji Temple — the five-story pagoda from every Kyoto photo
Philosopher's Path — 2km canal walk lined with cherry trees and temples
Higashiyama Jisho-ji (Silver Pavilion) — the understated counterpart to Kinkaku-ji

activities.name: Check out Osaka hotel, JR to Kyoto
Drop bags at Kyoto hotel (or use coin locker at station)

days.food: CHOICE (Higashiyama) — 100% vegan AND 100% gluten-free restaurant. Ramen, burgers, cakes — all safe. Gion Soy Milk Ramen — only dedicated GF ramen shop in Japan, rice noodles, celiac-certified.
days.tip: Kiyomizu-dera before 9am is magical. The wooden terrace juts out over a hillside — no nails, just interlocking beams. Sunset from here is extraordinary.

days.title: Kyoto — Mountain Temples & Markets
days.tagline: Hike between mountain temples, then hunt for treasures at Nishiki Market.
highlights: Kurama-Kibune mountain hike — 2-3 hrs through ancient forest
Kuramadera Temple at the start, Kifune Shrine at the finish
Lunch at Yoshuji — shōjin ryōri (Buddhist cuisine) in a farmhouse with fire pit
Afternoon: Nishiki Market — 400m of food stalls, Kyoto's kitchen
Nijo Castle — Tokugawa shogunate seat, famous 'nightingale floors'
Kyoto International Manga Museum if time permits

activities.name: Eizan Line back to central Kyoto
Dinner — Moon and Back Ramen (near Nishiki)

transport.note: Eizan Line from Demachiyanagi to Kurama/Kibune

days.food: Yoshuji (Kurama) — Buddhist vegetarian in a traditional farmhouse. Mostly naturally GF, English menu. Moon and Back Ramen — vegan ramen near Nishiki, GF rice noodles available (+¥275).
days.tip: The Kurama-Kibune trail is moderate but has some steep sections and exposed tree roots (the famous kinonesandō). Wear proper shoes. The hike is easier Kurama → Kibune (net downhill to the shrine).

days.title: Kyoto — Moss, Gold & Geisha
days.tagline: The temples the day-trippers never reach. Plus Gion at its most atmospheric.
highlights: Saihō-ji (Koke-dera) — the legendary moss temple, 130 species of moss
Mandatory sutra-copying meditation, then garden stroll
Sanjūsangendō — 1,001 life-size golden Kannon statues in one hall
Tōfuku-ji — massive Zen temple, autumn maple garden
Gion evening stroll — deeper into geisha culture than the day trip allowed

transport.note: Bus to Saihō-ji (Kokedera-Suzumushidera-mae stop), then city buses

days.food: TOUSUIRO Gion — GF kaiseki in a 130-year-old merchant house. ¥7,500 for the vegan 'Rokuhara' course. Book 3 days ahead for GF preparation.
days.tip: Saihō-ji REQUIRES advance reservation (2 months ahead, max 2 per booking). You'll copy Buddhist sutras in ink before seeing the garden — embrace it, it's incredibly meditative. The moss garden is worth every yen.
bookAhead: Saihō-ji (Koke-dera) — book at saihoji-kokedera.com, ¥4,000 + ¥110 fee, max 2 per booking

highlights: Shinkansen Kyoto → Odawara — 2 hrs
Buy Hakone Free Pass at Odawara (¥6,000/2 days — covers everything)
Hakone Tozan Railway up the mountain switchbacks
Settle into ryokan/hotel — onsen time!
Evening: first onsen experience. Remember: wash first, then soak. No swimwear.

activities.name: Buy Hakone Free Pass at Odawara Station
Ryokan dinner (if included) or Shika-jaya (tofu dishes)

days.tip: Hakone Free Pass is ESSENTIAL — covers trains, cable car, ropeway, boat, and buses for 2 days. Buy at Odawara.

rules: Wash COMPLETELY before entering the bath — use the small stools and buckets at the shower area
Enter fully naked — no swimwear allowed
Keep your small towel out of the water (fold it on your head)
Be quiet — onsens are for peaceful relaxation
If you have tattoos: ask first, but Hakone is generally more lenient than cities
onsenEtiquette.tip: Private baths (kashikiri) are available at most ryokan — perfect if you're nervous about communal bathing

days.title: Hakone — Hiking & Hot Springs
days.tagline: Volcanic valleys, sacred lakes, and the old Tokaido highway through cedar forests.
highlights: Old Tokaido Road hike — ancient cedar-lined stone path, 2-3 hrs
Owakudani — steaming volcanic valley, black eggs, sulphur vents
Hakone Ropeway over the caldera — spectacular views
Lake Ashi boat cruise — Mt Fuji reflected in the water (if clear)
Hakone Shrine & Kuzuryū Shrine — torii gate on the lake
Amasake Tea House — 400-year-old rest stop on the old highway

transport.note: All covered: ropeway, cable car, boat, buses

days.food: Amasake Tea House — 400-year-old thatched-roof stop on the Tokaido Road. Serves amazake (sweet fermented rice drink, naturally GF and vegan). The black eggs at Owakudani are NOT vegetarian (they're eggs). Pack snacks for the hike.
days.tip: Start the Tokaido Road hike early — the cedar avenue in morning light is magical. Take the bus to Hatajuku to skip the boring road section. Owakudani may close if volcanic activity increases — check on the day.

days.title: Hakone → Matsumoto
days.tagline: From volcanic hot springs to samurai castle. The Japanese Alps are calling.
highlights: Train Hakone-Yumoto → Odawara → Shinjuku → Matsumoto — ~4 hrs
Matsumoto Castle — Japan's oldest five-tier castle, a National Treasure
Nawate-dōri shopping street — retro frog-themed lane along the river
Evening: soba noodles — Matsumoto's specialty (buckwheat = naturally GF!)

activities.name: Arrive Matsumoto, check into hotel, lunch

days.food: Takagi Soba — 100% buckwheat soba noodles (naturally GF). Near the castle. They're very knowledgeable about gluten. Asian Station — Nepalese/Indian, vegan curries, extremely dietary-friendly, #8 rated in Matsumoto. Book ahead, small restaurant.
days.tip: Matsumoto Castle is Japan's oldest five-tiered castle. The stairs inside are STEEP — almost ladders. It's worth climbing to the top for the mountain views. Arrive before 3pm to avoid the rush.

days.title: Nakasendo Trail — Magome to Tsumago
days.tagline: Walk the 400-year-old postal road through mountain forests. Edo-period Japan, preserved.
days.stay: Matsumoto hotel (or overnight in Tsumago for full immersion)
highlights: Bus Matsumoto → Nakatsugawa → Magome — ~1.5 hrs
Hike the Nakasendo trail: Magome → Tsumago — 8 km, 2-3 hrs
Cobblestone paths through cedar forests, waterfalls, rice paddies
Magome Pass (801m) — the highest point, then gentle descent
Tsumago-juku — perfectly preserved Edo-period post town
Return to Matsumoto (or stay in Tsumago ryokan)

activities.name: Pack hiking snacks from konbini (onigiri, edamame, fruit)
Bus/train to Nakatsugawa, then bus to Magome
Lunch in Tsumago — gohei mochi (grilled rice dumplings, vegan)

transport.note: Bus to Magome, hike to Tsumago, bus+train back to Matsumoto

days.food: Pack snacks before leaving! On the trail: Tateba-jaya serves free matcha at the midpoint. In Tsumago: gohei mochi — grilled rice dumplings with sesame/walnut sauce, naturally GF and vegan (confirm no fish broth). Tawaraya and Yoshimuraya in Tsumago for soba.
days.tip: Walk Magome → Tsumago (not the reverse) — it's net downhill after the pass. The cobblestones are VERY slippery when wet, bring proper hiking shoes. Send your big luggage ahead via coin lockers or takkyubin. This is one of Japan's most beautiful walks — take your time.

Snacks from konbini (onigiri, edamame, fruit, rice crackers)

restaurants.note: Extra restaurant recommendations for extended trip locations. The couple has celiac-level gluten allergy — GF safety is critical. They're less experienced with Japan, so detailed guidance matters more.

spots.name: CHOICE
spots.mustTry: Everything — 100% vegan AND 100% gluten-free establishment. Ramen, burgers, cakes, all safe.
spots.note: Entirely dedicated vegan/GF restaurant. 32 seats. Closed Thursdays.

spots.name: Gion Soy Milk Ramen
spots.mustTry: Soy milk ramen with rice noodles — the only dedicated GF ramen restaurant in Japan
spots.note: Celiac-certified. Also has GF gyoza, curry rice, and vegan cakes. 11:00-20:30 daily.

spots.name: TOUSUIRO Gion
spots.mustTry: Vegan kaiseki 'Rokuhara' course (¥7,500) — multi-course Japanese haute cuisine in a 130-year-old merchant house
spots.note: Requires advance reservation (3 days for GF preparation). A once-in-a-lifetime meal.

spots.name: Moon and Back Ramen Bar
spots.mustTry: Spicy Tandan Ramen — white sesame broth with bok choy and tofu skin
spots.note: GF rice noodles available (+¥275 surcharge). Two Kyoto locations.

spots.name: Yoshuji
spots.mustTry: Vegetarian noodle bowls and set lunch in a traditional farmhouse with irori fire pit
spots.note: 3 min from Kurama Station. English menu. Mostly naturally GF. Closed Tuesdays. Call ahead to confirm GF.

hakone.label: Hakone

spots.name: Nukafuku
spots.mustTry: Rice bran donuts — rotating daily flavors, all 100% GF
spots.note: Owner speaks excellent English and understands celiac. Also has vegan sausages, smoothies, dango. Takeaway only.

spots.name: Shika-jaya
spots.mustTry: Okabe Zen course — fully vegan tofu set
spots.note: Bring your own tamari — standard soy sauce has wheat. Staff experienced with modifications. Closed Thursdays.

hakone.survivalTips: Hakone is tough for GF. Most restaurants use standard soy sauce and dashi. Your best bets: Nukafuku (100% GF, Gora area), ryokan meals (request GF 2+ weeks ahead), and konbini onigiri. Pack tamari packets and GF snacks from Kyoto before arriving. The Amasake Tea House on the Old Tokaido Road serves amazake (fermented rice drink) which is naturally GF and vegan.

matsumoto.label: Matsumoto & Nakasendo

spots.name: Takagi Soba
spots.mustTry: Juwari soba (100% buckwheat noodles) — naturally GF. Request plain or with salt instead of soy sauce.
spots.note: Buckwheat is NOT wheat — it's naturally gluten-free. This shop uses 100% buckwheat, no wheat filler. Staff very knowledgeable.

spots.name: Asian Station
spots.nameJp: アジアンステーション
spots.mustTry: Vegan curry with rice — naturally GF. Excellent naan but skip it (wheat).
spots.note: #8 of 998 restaurants on TripAdvisor, 4.9 rating. Only a few tables — book ahead. Owner very allergy-aware.

spots.name: Menshoshinbusakiya
spots.nameJp: 麺小新ぶさきや 松本店
spots.mustTry: Vegan ramen with brown rice noodles — specifically designed for celiac diners
spots.note: Staff extremely knowledgeable about celiac disease. Small chain with 4 locations in Japan.

matsumoto.survivalTips: Matsumoto is surprisingly good for GF because of its soba culture — 100% buckwheat (juwari) soba is naturally GF. Always confirm 'juwari' (十割) not 'nihachi' (二八, which is 80% buckwheat + 20% wheat). On the Nakasendo trail: pack ALL food from konbini before starting. The only trail stop is Tateba-jaya which offers free matcha (GF). In Tsumago: gohei mochi (grilled rice on a stick with sesame/walnut sauce) is naturally GF and vegan — confirm no fish broth.

forLessExperienced: Always carry your allergy card (allergyCardJp from the main restaurants section) — show it to every restaurant
Download HappyCow and FindMeGlutenFree apps before leaving
Google Translate camera mode — point your phone at any menu for instant translation
7-Eleven ATMs give the best exchange rate and have English menus
IC card (Suica/Pasmo) works on ALL trains, metros, buses, and in konbini
Konbini onigiri (rice balls) are your emergency food — umeboshi, kombu, natto fillings are GF and vegan
Japan runs on cash more than you'd expect — always have ¥10,000+ on you
Trains run EXACTLY on time. If the schedule says 10:32, it leaves at 10:32.
Bow when someone bows to you. Say 'sumimasen' (excuse me) and 'arigatou gozaimasu' (thank you)
Shoes off in temples, ryokans, and many restaurants — wear socks without holes
emergencyFood: 7-Eleven: onigiri (rice balls), edamame, plain rice, fruit, salad
FamilyMart: GF rice crackers (senbei), mochi, banana, boiled eggs
Lawson: yakiimo (roasted sweet potato) in season, fruit cups
Any supermarket after 7pm: bento boxes 30-50% off — look for rice-based ones
practicalTips.jrPassNote: With the extended route (Kyoto → Hakone → Matsumoto → Tokyo), buying a 7-day JR Pass (¥50,000) might actually make sense for the extended couple. Their shinkansen Kyoto→Odawara alone is ¥11,000, plus trains to Matsumoto (¥6,620) and local trains. Calculate before buying.
